h1: San Elizario, Clint, Anthony & Vinton Court Ticket Lawyer — El Paso, TX
intro: El Paso County's smallest cities each run their own municipal court, often with only one or two docket days a month. That makes a missed date costly and a lawyer unusually valuable. Attorney Robert Navar handles San Elizario, Clint, Anthony and Vinton tickets for a flat $69.
summary: San Elizario, Clint, Anthony and Vinton each have a small municipal court that hears Class C citations written by that city's own police or marshal, typically on a limited docket schedule of one or two days a month.
Our flat fee in any of these four courts is $69 per citation; extra tickets from the same stop are discounted add-ons. Hire online or call 915-503-1600.
Because dockets are so infrequent, missing a date can mean a warrant and weeks of waiting. We file the appearance and attend the docket so you do not have to.
The same Texas options apply: dismissal, deferred disposition under art. 45.051, or a driving safety course dismissal under art. 45.0511 where the court allows it.
Sheriff, DPS and constable tickets in these towns go to an El Paso County JP precinct instead — the issuing agency on the citation decides the court.

sections.heading: Why Small-Town Courts Make a Lawyer Worth More, Not Less
paragraphs: A ticket from a small city feels minor, but the courts that handle them are the hardest for a driver to deal with alone. San Elizario, Clint, Anthony and Vinton each hold court only on scheduled days — often one or two a month — with a part-time judge and a prosecutor who may serve several towns. The clerk's office keeps limited hours. If you miss the appearance date, or show up on a day court is not in session, the next chance may be a month away, and by then the court may have issued a warrant and added a failure-to-appear charge under Transportation Code 543.009.

Our office handles all four courts for the same flat fee we charge in Horizon City and Socorro. We file the appearance before your date, track each court's docket calendar, and attend when the case is called. Robert Navar has practiced in El Paso County for more than ten years and knows how each of these courts prefers to resolve a traffic case. Verify current addresses and docket schedules with the individual court if you plan to go yourself — they change — or let us confirm them for you.

One caution that applies to all four towns: the city police or marshal's tickets go to the municipal court, but tickets written by Sheriff's deputies, DPS troopers and constables on the same roads go to an El Paso County Justice of the Peace precinct. Check the issuing agency on your citation, or use our free ticket and warrant lookup.

sections.heading: San Elizario Municipal Court
paragraphs: San Elizario is the Lower Valley town just past Socorro on Socorro Rd, and its police department writes tickets on Socorro Rd, Alameda Ave (Highway 20) and the farm roads between them. The San Elizario Municipal Court hears those citations on a limited schedule. Speeding through the historic district, stop-sign violations and compliance charges like no insurance and expired registration are the typical cases we see.

San Elizario's court, like its neighbors, generally allows deferred disposition for ordinary moving violations and dismisses compliance tickets when the driver shows the problem was fixed. We ask every client to send a current insurance card and registration before the docket so we can request a dismissal rather than a deferral where possible.

sections.heading: Clint Municipal Court
paragraphs: Clint sits east of Socorro along Alameda Ave and FM 1110, with I-10 passing just north of town. The Town of Clint's police write citations on Alameda, on the FM 1110 approach to the interstate and in the school zones serving Clint ISD, and those tickets go to Clint Municipal Court. Many drivers ticketed in Clint live in Horizon City or far-east El Paso and are passing through, which is why forgotten Clint tickets are a common source of warrants and OMNI holds.

Clint's docket is infrequent, so when we file an appearance we also calendar the next setting and handle any continuance within the flat fee. For school-zone speeding, where the court is less willing to offer a course dismissal, we negotiate for deferred disposition or a non-moving reduction.

sections.heading: Anthony Municipal Court
paragraphs: Anthony, Texas is at the far northwest corner of the county on the New Mexico line, where I-10 and Highway 20 (Doniphan Dr) cross into Anthony, New Mexico. The Town of Anthony's police patrol Franklin St, Doniphan Dr and the frontage roads near the I-10 exit, and their citations go to Anthony Municipal Court. Out-of-town drivers headed to Las Cruces and commercial drivers on I-10 are a large share of the court's traffic cases.

Commercial drivers deserve a special note: a CDL holder cannot use deferred disposition or a driving safety course to mask a Class C conviction, so Anthony cases for truckers turn on the citation's defects and on negotiating a charge that does not count as a serious violation. Tell us at intake if you hold a CDL. The nearby El Paso County JP precinct serving Anthony and Canutillo handles trooper and deputy tickets on the same roads; we appear in both.

sections.heading: Vinton Municipal Court
paragraphs: Vinton is the small Upper Valley village between Canutillo and Anthony along Doniphan Dr and Vinton Rd, with I-10 running along its edge. The Village of Vinton's officers write tickets on Vinton Rd, Doniphan Dr and the I-10 frontage roads, and those citations go to Vinton Municipal Court, which holds court on a limited schedule like its neighbors. Speeding on Doniphan and compliance stops are the typical cases.

Vinton is the smallest of the four courts, and a missed date can take the longest to fix on your own. We file the appearance, request a recall of any warrant that has already issued — see traffic warrant recall — and ask the court to set the ticket on its next docket. From there the case is negotiated for dismissal, deferred disposition or a course dismissal like any other.

sections.heading: Our $69 Flat Fee and What to Do Now
paragraphs: We charge $69 per citation in San Elizario, Clint, Anthony and Vinton Municipal Courts. The fee covers the appearance, every docket setting and the closing paperwork; court fees for a deferral or course are paid to the court separately. Extra citations from the same stop are $10–$30 add-ons at checkout, and warrants are $35 for the first plus $20 for each additional. Measured against a conviction — two points and three years of higher insurance — the fee is the cheaper choice in nearly every case.

Do not pay the ticket, do not request defensive driving yourself, and do not wait for a docket date that may be a month out. Send us the citation through the online form or call 915-503-1600. The consultation is free and se habla español. This page is general information, not legal advice about your case.

faqs.q: Which court has my ticket if I was stopped in Clint or San Elizario?
faqs.a: If a city police officer wrote it, that city's municipal court. If a Sheriff's deputy, DPS trooper or constable wrote it, an El Paso County Justice of the Peace precinct. The issuing agency is printed on the citation, and our free lookup form can confirm it.

faqs.q: How often do these courts hold traffic dockets?
faqs.a: Typically only one or two days a month, with limited clerk hours in between. Verify the current schedule with the specific court. Because the gaps are long, we file your appearance right away so a missed date does not turn into a warrant.

faqs.q: What is the attorney fee for Anthony or Vinton tickets?
faqs.a: A flat $69 per citation in any of the four courts. Additional citations from the same stop are discounted add-ons, and warrant recalls are $35 for the first warrant and $20 for each additional one.

faqs.q: Do I have to drive out to the court?
faqs.a: In most cases, no. We appear for you on the docket day and negotiate with the prosecutor. A personal appearance is needed only if the case is set for trial, which is rare.

faqs.q: I got the ticket passing through on I-10 and I live out of state. Can you still help?
faqs.a: Yes. Out-of-town and out-of-state drivers are a large share of Anthony and Vinton cases. We handle the entire case by phone and email, and you never have to return to El Paso County.

faqs.q: I missed my court date in one of these towns months ago. What now?
faqs.a: There is likely a warrant and possibly an OMNI hold on your license renewal. Call us the same day. We file the appearance, request the recall and get the ticket onto the next docket — see traffic warrant recall.
